title: Grünfeld Defense: the ideas
line: Black strikes at the center with a pawn at once, then hits White's pawns with the bishop, a side pawn and the queen.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Bring the knight out. For now it stops White's other center pawn from coming to e4.
Push the pawn on g7 one square, to make room for your bishop.

also.e7e6: That leads to the Nimzo-Indian or the Queen's Indian, also sound. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares, before White's pawn can come to e4.

also.f8g7: That is the King's Indian Defense, also sound. This lesson goes on with the pawn.

steps.after: This is the Grünfeld Defense. Here White brings a bishop out, one of several choices; the next lessons show the main ones.

steps.text: Put the bishop on the long diagonal. Once your knight moves, it aims at White's pawn on d4.
Strike at the pawn on d4 with the pawn on c7.
Bring the queen out. It pins the knight to White's king and eyes the pawn on c5.
steps.after: Black usually gets the pawn back within a few moves.

summary: Black stakes a claim in the center at once, then hits White's pawns with the bishop, a side pawn and the queen.
